identity: Classical Arabic philosophical narrative-argument: the section of Ibn Tufayl's Hayy ibn Yaqzan in which Hayy, at the close of his fifth seven-year period (age 35, stated explicitly at tokens 184-191), completes his inference to the Necessary Existent, then turns inward and proves that the faculty by which he grasps It is neither a body nor a power in a body, and therefore incorruptible. Register: medieval expository-narrative prose in the third person, built out of long periodic sentences chained with fa- and wa-, punctuated by rhetorical questions, scholastic enumerations (the five senses, the attributes of perfection, potential vs actual perception), and worked examples introduced by mithl. The <NL> structure is an editor's paragraphing, and it already isolates many of the largest discourse steps: paragraphs open with fa-lamma, wa-qad kana tabayyana, wa-kadhalika, wa-amma, wa-hadhihi. But paragraphs are NOT sentences: P14 (801-920, 120 tokens) demonstrably holds three complete periods, so genuine intra-paragraph segmentation is required.
law: A boundary falls at the last token of a complete predication when the next token opens a NEW independent predication that constitutes a fresh discourse step rather than a continuation of the same step. Operationally, in this text: (1) fa- + a verb of cognition or investigation that states the next move or the conclusion drawn from what precedes (fa-alima, fa-tabayyana lahu bi-dhalika, fa-zahara lahu bi-dhalika, fa-tasaffaha, fa-ra-a where it opens rather than completes a move) closes the preceding sentence; likewise the inferential connectives fa-idhan and fa-la when they draw the conclusion of a finished argument. (2) Discourse openers that this editor demonstrably treats as sentence-initial, because they open whole paragraphs elsewhere in the document, are stops when they occur paragraph-internally: dhalika li-anna, wa-qad + perfect, wa-kadhalika, wa-li-dhalika, wa-amma, thumma inna, and any asyndetic nominal restart (hadha huwa ...). (3) A rhetorical or deliberative question terminates at its own last token; the declarative that follows is a new sentence. (4) Subordinators hold the sentence open and never license a stop before them: hatta, bare li-anna, idha, in / wa-in when it is not restarting a bifurcation with its own illustration, ka-ma anna, and the exemplifying mithl + example, which attaches to the generalization it illustrates. (5) wa- + verb with the same subject inside the same narrative move is a comma; wa- + a shifted topic, or a repeated head-noun that restarts the inquiry, is a stop. (6) Enumerative and appositional lists stay inside one sentence: the five senses and their objects, the cascade of divine predicates, and a Qur'anic tag joined by wa- are all sentence-internal, not stops.
reasoning: MANDATORY SPINE: the 16 tokens preceding each <NL> (27, 84, 105, 174, 256, 355, 420, 469, 524, 607, 628, 716, 799, 920, 939, 1009) and the final token 1031 are fixed and verified against the tokenization; no <NL> itself carries a boundary. [64 vs 65] the mahma-clause is complete at 'wa-min fi'lihi'; the second fa-alima introduces a substantively new conclusion (God's transcendence over what emanates from Him), not a restatement, so a stop; med. [115] the tracing of the attributes of deficiency finishes at 'wa-munazzahan anha' and a rhetorical question opens; hi. [130] I take the two wa-kayfa questions as two questions, not one coordinated question: the first carries its own hal-ground (the meaning of deficiency is sheer privation) and the second builds ON that ground, so each closes with its own terminator; med, this is the weakest of the three P4 sites. [148] the second question closes at 'wujudahu' and 'fa-la wujuda illa huwa' is the declarative conclusion; hi. [168 NO BOUNDARY] the isolated single-letter token 'w' at 169 is an artifact of quotation bracketing around the Qur'anic tag, not evidence of a stop; that wa- coordinates the tag INTO the cascade 'fa-huwa al-wujud wa-huwa al-kamal ... wa-huwa huwa', so the cascade and the tag are one sentence. [191] 'wa-dhalika khamsatun wa-thalathuna aman' is a closing parenthetical gloss on the date; wa-qad + perfect then opens a new sentence, and this editor opens paragraphs with exactly that formula at 422, 471 and 922; hi. [556] the genuinely 50/50 site: syntactically wa-nazara is a third wa-coordinated verb in the fa-lamma apodosis (hana / wa-ja'ala yatafakkaru / wa-nazara), which argues for no stop, but the repeated head 'tilka al-dhat al-sharifa' -> 'dhatihi tilka al-sharifa' reads as a restart of the inquiry rather than a continuation, and what follows is a self-contained deliberative question; included at lo. [572] the hal-question closes and fa-ra-a answers it; hi. [603] 'hadha huwa ma'na al-fasad' is asyndetic and nominal, the clearest stop type in the document; hi. [679, 692, 702, 710 NO BOUNDARIES] the eye illustration is one comma-linked exposition: mithl al-'ayn ... fa-innaha ... wa-ma'na ... wa-fi hal fathiha ... wa-ma'na ...; I attach mithl to the generalization it illustrates, and 757 ('mithl man khuliqa makfufa al-basar', unambiguously mid-sentence because wa-in kanat follows) confirms that mithl does not start sentences here. [761] the second arm 'wa-in kanat qad adrakat bi-l-fi'l' is 38 tokens long and carries its own mithl-illustration; this editor separates the arms of a bifurcation elsewhere (the amma/fa-hadha division is split across the <NL> at 1010), so I stop here; med. [814] the general proportionality law closes at 'a'zam' and wa-li-dhalika opens the applied inference; hi. [839] that inference closes at 'al-shamm' and fa-in kana opens a fresh conditional period; hi. [840-920 NO INTERNAL BOUNDARIES] one giant conditional: protasis (fa-in kana ... wa-huwa fawqa ... wa-laysa fi al-wujud ...), apodosis (fa-man faqada ... fa-la mahalata ...), plus the ka-ma anna comparison, all held open by their subordinators. [956] wa-tabayyana lahu closes at 'li-fasadiha' and fa-zahara lahu bi-dhalika opens the consequence; med, treated identically to 481. [998 NO BOUNDARY] 'fa-hadha idha faraqa al-badan' is the resumptive apodosis of the fa-imma branch, sentence-internal. RESULT: 40 boundaries over 1016 non-<NL> tokens, mean sentence length about 25 tokens, which matches the three independently verifiable periods in P14 (14 / 25 / 81).
